what: phase 12.7 closed loop: two OS processes, ITCH over UDP as MoldUDP64, OUCH over SoupBinTCP, strategy fills recognised from its own feed

pacing.note: paced, not free-running -- about 62 seconds for a full ITCH session including pre- and post-market. Long enough to be evidence about the periodic path as well: SoupBinTCP heartbeats are sent from tick() and nowhere else, and a server declares its client dead after 15 seconds of silence, so a 62-second run ending with both processes exiting 0 could not have happened if tick() had stopped firing.

notes: WHAT THE AGREEING SHARE COUNTS PROVE, PRECISELY. split.hpp:376 does `c_.strategy_shares_taken += take;` and then `emit_exec(p, sref, take)` -- the same `take`. So these are one quantity measured twice, at the source and again after a round trip, NOT two independent computations; an earlier version of this file said otherwise and was wrong. What the agreement establishes is that every share the exchange put on the tape survived encoding, MoldUDP64 framing, a real UDP socket, sequencing, parsing, ownership attribution and the in-book test, with none dropped and none double-counted. It is not evidence that the quantity is arithmetically right: conserves_shares and agrees_with_book speak to that, and are recorded separately above.

taker_shares_invisible_to_itch is not an error. ITCH describes what happens to RESTING orders, so a strategy order that crosses is never named on the tape and cannot be seen this way. It is the difference between what OUCH reported and what the feed could show.

WHY THERE ARE TWO RUNS. my_refs is populated from OUCH Accepted, over TCP; both the ITCH Add and the ITCH Execution go out over UDP; and nothing orders those two transports against each other. An earlier version of this run disagreed with the exchange by exactly 202 shares while every datagram arrived and the sequencer reported nothing lost -- three fills reached the strategy before the acknowledgement naming their orders, and were dropped because the strategy did not yet know they were its own. Fills are now parked with everything the feed knew at the time and retired when the ack lands, and TCP is drained before UDP so the loop stops manufacturing the race out of nothing.

That second change made the first one invisible: the natural run now reports 0 races, which is the right outcome and useless as evidence. The acknowledgements_held_250ms run forces it. There, 1178 of 1200 Adds and 1679 of the fills -- 84407 shares, 79.5% of the total -- arrive before the acknowledgement that names them, and the counts still agree with the exchange exactly. Every one of those shares would have been silently lost before the fix.

Neither run is deterministic and neither is meant to be. The fill count depends on how stale the strategy's view of the book is when each order lands, which depends on scheduling. What is asserted is the agreement between the two processes and the absence of gaps, not the particular number of fills.

udp_rcvbuf_granted is what the kernel actually gave, not what was asked for. The request is 8MB; Linux clamps it to net.core.rmem_max and says nothing, which on this machine means 416 KB. That is what stands between an unpaced feed and a dropped datagram, so it is recorded rather than assumed. Both runs here are paced and neither lost one.

The four-arm gate that establishes the fills came from the feed and not from OUCH runs on generated feeds in CI: scripts/closed-loop-check.sh. Six mutations were run against it and all six were caught.
